label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
**Northvale froze your withdrawals. Here is what happened and what you can do.**

*Inês, 10 November 2026*

Since Friday 6 November at 09:00, you can't take your money out of Pinha. If you've been refreshing the app, writing to us, or lying awake doing maths about rent, I know. I'm writing this because Rui is on calls with lawyers and Banco de Portugal all day, and because I write most of what you read in the app anyway. This one is the hardest I've written.

I'm furious. Mostly at Northvale, and a bit at us. You're allowed to be angry too, and I'm not going to tell you to stay calm.

**What happened**

Northvale Payments, the e-money institution in Vilnius that holds the money for Pinha's ~14,200 users, sent us an email on Wednesday 4 November. It said they were ending our contract for "commercial" reasons, with 30 days' notice. The only explanation was a "risk appetite review". No specific reason, nothing we could respond to.

Thirty days' notice means thirty days to move everything over in an orderly way. Two days later, on Friday at 09:00, they blocked all outgoing transfers. No warning. Deposits and round-ups stopped as well, so nothing is going in or out right now.

That is not what their own notice said. Call it a "risk appetite review" if you like. To me it looks like a company that decided to get out and left the people holding the bag to deal with it. Their account manager stopped answering our calls on Friday, and their number now goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian.

**Where your money is**

Your money has not disappeared. Northvale holds it in a safeguarded account that is separate from Northvale's own money, and they cannot use it for their own purposes.

The problem is that we can't move it either. Only Northvale can release it, and so far they haven't.

I'm not going to write "your money is safe" in big friendly letters and leave it there. It's in a safeguarded account, that's true, and it is also true that you can't reach it. Both things are real.

**What we're doing**

- **A new partner.** We've already signed with Ostra Bank in Lisbon. To move your balances over, we need two things: Northvale has to send us the file with everyone's balances, and Banco de Portugal has to approve the migration.
- **Complaints.** On Saturday 7 November we filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and with the Lithuanian central bank, which supervises Northvale.
- **Lawyers.** Rui is on calls with them and with Banco de Portugal today, and will be again.
- **Individual releases.** For people with urgent situations, we're asking Northvale to release specific balances one by one. I can't tell you they'll say yes. We're trying.

**How long will this take?**

Our estimate is 10 to 15 working days. It is an estimate, not a promise. Two of the steps depend entirely on other people, and one of those people has stopped picking up the phone. I won't give you a date we might miss, because you'd plan your life around it and I'd be the one who broke it.

What I can promise is that we'll tell you what's happening, good or bad, as it happens.

**What you can do now**

1. **If it's urgent**, write to **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE**. By urgent I mean things like rent, medical costs, or losing your job. Tell us what the deadline is, what happens if you miss it, and the email address you use for Pinha. This is the group we're pushing hardest for with Northvale. I can't promise every case will be released, but every case will be read.

   One of you wrote to us in capital letters, and she was right to. She's been saving for three years for a car deposit, and the dealership gives her until Friday 13 November. I read that on the metro and nearly cried. If you're in a spot like hers, with a hard date, write to the urgent address and put the date in the first line.

2. **If it's not urgent**, you don't need to do anything today. Your money stays where it is, and when the migration happens, your balance moves with it. You don't need to re-register or send us documents for that.

3. **If you've already written to us**, we have your email. Since Friday 6 November we've received about 1,900, and three of us are answering them. Replies are currently taking about two days, which is too slow, and I know it. We're going through them in order, with the urgent ones first.

4. **Don't pay anything to anyone** who contacts you offering to "unlock" your funds. We will never ask you for your password, your PIN or a payment to get your money out. When a situation like this hits the news, scammers show up. Be careful with any message, from anyone, that you didn't start.

5. **Check back here.** We'll post an update every Monday and Thursday on this blog until this is resolved, even when the update is "nothing has changed". The next one is Thursday 12 November.

We've also cancelled the monthly fee for November and December for everyone. I'm not presenting that as a gift. It's the minimum, and it doesn't fix anything.

**Our part in this**

Northvale did this, and it's on them. But I won't pretend we have nothing to answer for.

We had one payments partner and no backup. We trusted a single company with everything, and when that company walked away, we had nowhere to go. We were naive, it's our mistake, and I'm sorry. Ostra Bank is the first step. We'll also explain how we plan to make sure this can't happen again, once your money is out and moved.

I designed the screen in the app that says "your money is always yours, take it out anytime". I look at it now and feel sick. I believed it when I made it, and it wasn't true when you needed it to be. I'm not going to hide behind "it's the partner's fault". The promise was ours.

**What I'd like you to take from this**

- Your money is held in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale's own funds. It is not lost.
- You can't withdraw until Northvale releases the balances and Banco de Portugal approves the move to Ostra Bank.
- Our estimate is 10 to 15 working days. That is not a promise.
- If it's urgent, write to urgent@pinha.example with **URGENTE** in the subject.
- Updates are every Monday and Thursday, here.

You trusted us with money you worked for. We're going to keep working on this until every euro of it is back in your hands, and we'll tell you the truth along the way, even when it's ugly.

Inês
Product design, Pinha

---

A few things to check before you publish:

- **Date.** My system shows today as 11 November, but you said Tuesday 10 November, so I used the 10th and made the next update Thursday 12 November. Change it if you post later.
- **The Porto user.** I left out the city and her name. Ask her before using her story, even this anonymised.
- **"Looks like a company that decided to get out."** I kept the anger but phrased it as how it looks to you rather than calling them cowards outright. Please run the Northvale paragraph past Rui or the lawyers, since a public statement about them can have legal consequences.
- **10 to 15 working days.** I didn't say when the count starts, because I don't know. If it's from the moment Northvale sends the file, say so.
- **Things I added that you didn't list.** The scam warning, the "no need to re-register" line, and the advice on what to put in an urgent email. Delete any that aren't true for how Pinha works.
- **Ostra Bank "migration doesn't need anything from users."** I assumed that from your notes. Check it's right.
